correctness.rationale: Uniformly naming the n chords yields exchangeable double-occurrence words, whose restrictions to any k marked chords are uniform among (2k)!/2^k words. The 90 three-label words give probabilities (1/3,2/5,1/5,1/15). For two triple sets sharing r=1,2,3 labels, exactly enumerating all words on 6-r labels yields Q1 of denominator 2835, Q2 of denominator 315 and Q3 of denominator 15; disjoint supports are independent. Summing covariance of triple indicators gives comb(n,3)*sum_{r=1}^3 comb(3,r)comb(n-3,3-r)*(Q_r-qq^T), equivalent to displayed quadratic matrix expression. Independent enumeration of all 113400,2520,90 double-occurrence words reproduced all 48 table entries. A separately coded symbolic interpolation checked every matrix component at n=3,4,5,6,17,118,119 and recovered the exact N1,N2 numerator n^2-115n-420. Its root lies strictly between 118 and 119 (n=118 -> -66, n=119 -> 56), establishing sharp sign via monotonic quadratic for all n>=3. Finite verification is exhaustive for the finite Q_r tables needed for the infinite-n overlap identity, not an extrapolation in n.

value.rationale: PASS: Full joint second-moment classification of all four induced three-vertex graph types in a canonical random circle graph is a natural complete finite-motif invariant. The highly nonobvious negative-to-positive covariance transition at exactly 119 chords demonstrates a structural dependence reversal not predicted by fixed-triple exclusion, and the finite-overlap derivation is useful for further random chord motif studies.

final_claim: For a uniform n-chord perfect matching of 2n cyclic endpoints, n>=3, the counts of induced three-chord subgraphs with j=0,1,2,3 crossings have exact mean comb(n,3)*(1/3,2/5,1/5,1/15) and covariance comb(n,3)*(n^2*A+n*B+C)/9450 for explicit four-by-four integer matrices A,B,C. In particular Cov(N1,N2)=comb(n,3)*(n^2-115n-420)/9450, negative for n<=118 and positive for n>=119.
limitations: n>=3, uniform fixed cyclic endpoint perfect matchings; not arbitrary graph models or independently sampled chord endpoints.
Complete induced 3-motif covariance only, no stronger joint distribution or CLT; priority best-of-knowledge.
